decisions.reason: Step 3.1 uses sigma without defining a cyclic permutation; interpreting it as the von Neumann successor would not produce a finite cycle. The core common-positive-period proof in steps 1.1 and 2.1 is sound independently. Replaced the ambiguous cycle notation by explicit transitions x_j to x_((j+1) mod k) and computed diagonal powers, giving exactly the positive multiples of k. This is a local illustrative notation defect, not a failure of the definition.

The whole-sample-space assertion in step 2.2 is false: the path at omega=a hits A at time zero, whereas the path at omega=b never hits A. The preceding deterministic-start construction already assigns probability one to {b} under P_b, so the asserted hitting probability and nonuniqueness conclusion are correct. Replaced the erroneous universal phrase with the exact path omega=b and P_b({b})=1; this is a local quantifier slip with no change to the witness or conclusion.
